craft_claim: Legitimate urgency tracks a real, locatable exigence whose resolution is still possible; when the pressure originates in the rhetoric rather than the situation, the tone becomes manufactured.

supporting_evidence.location: The Rhetorical Situation, pp. 1-14 (exigence as the organizing element of the situation)
supporting_evidence.note: Bitzer defines rhetorical discourse as called into existence by a situation containing an exigence: an imperfection that can be positively modified by discourse. This gives the tone a test for real versus staged pressure.

supporting_evidence.location: Toward a Sophistic Definition of Rhetoric, pp. 35-48 (kairos)
supporting_evidence.note: The Sophistic treatment ties effective speech to the opportune moment (kairos) and to appropriateness (prepon); urgency is legitimate when the moment is genuinely opportune, not when the moment is asserted.

counterevidence.location: The Myth of the Rhetorical Situation, pp. 154-161
counterevidence.note: Vatz argues that rhetoric makes situations salient rather than being determined by them. This is the precise mechanism by which urgency can be fabricated: the rhetor manufactures salience and then claims the situation demanded it.

scope: Persuasive, informational and fiction prose in which urgency is claimed as a reason to act.
exceptions: Openly fictional dramatized clocks (a countdown invented for a story) are not deception when the fiction frame is clear.
Satire or critique of marketing urgency may perform manufactured pressure deliberately, with the performance as the object of critique.
